Tampere University is a unique, boldly future‑oriented and evolving community, and one of Finland’s most multidisciplinary universities. At Tampere University, technology, health and society come together in a distinctive way. Our research groups and projects carry out interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral research that transcends organisational boundaries. Our community is international, with members from more than 80 countries. Read more at
https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau
.
DETECTIVE
(Data-driven Excellence in Training of Epidemiological, Clinical, Technological and Innovative Virus Experts) is a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. The network brings together leading academic, public health, clinical, and industrial partners across Europe to train the next generation of researchers in epidemic intelligence, emerging virus surveillance, and pandemic preparedness. Through interdisciplinary research and international collaboration, DETECTIVE aims to improve the early detection of emerging pathogens, strengthen risk assessment, and support real-time, evidence-based public health decision-making. For more information, please visit:
virusdetective.eu
From wastewater to data-driven epidemic prediction
Background of Project DC9
The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated how public health measures and changes in population behaviour can influence viral circulation. Following the lifting of restrictions, many viruses showed unusual rebounds and altered seasonal patterns, but these effects remain poorly understood across the broader virome. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE), combined with viral enrichment and high-throughput sequencing, provides a powerful approach for monitoring community-level virus circulation across a broad range of pathogens. This doctoral project will integrate wastewater virome data with epidemiological and other population-level data to investigate viral dynamics during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The study is based on a unique longitudinal dataset of monthly wastewater samples collected from Finnish cities. The project will move from wastewater virome monitoring to data-driven models for epidemic prediction and public health action. By combining comprehensive viral surveillance with advanced data analysis and predictive modelling, the research will provide new insights into viral epidemiology and contribute to the development of wastewater-based early-warning systems for future epidemics and pandemics.
Job Description and Research Objectives:
At Tampere University, DETECTIVE is looking for a Doctoral Candidate 9 to work on Work Package 2.
As Doctoral Candidate 9, you will:
– Build a longitudinal wastewater virome surveillance system
– Apply, qPCR and capture enrichment and high-throughput sequencing to profile all vertebrate-infecting viruses, including human and potential zoonotic pathogens.
– Assess relationships between wastewater viral loads and clinical indicators, including seasonality, early surges, and viral interference.
– Create bioinformatic pipelines for sensitive detection and full-genome recovery
– Develop data-driven models for epidemic prediction, vaccination strategy, and integration of multi-virus WBE into public-health early-warning systems.
Supervisory Team
The DC will be supervised by:
– Assoc. Prof Sami Oikarinen
– Dr. Ana Da Silva Filipe
Additional scientific mentoring and collaboration will be provided by:
– Assoc. Prof Jaana Jurvansuu from the Tampere University
Planned Secondments
The doctoral candidate will undertake international secondments within the DETECTIVE network, including:
– UoG-CVR with Dr. Ana Da Silva Filipe
– QCMD with Dr. Elaine McCulloc
These secondments will provide exposure to both academic and industrial research environments and offer opportunities to develop complementary scientific and transferable skills.
Requirements
We are looking for a motivated researcher with a relevant Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, bioinformatics, microbiology, virology, immunology, epidemiology, or a related field. Experience with molecular technologies and bioinformatics will be considered an advantage. The successful candidate should be highly motivated to develop expertise in data science, including machine learning and artificial intelligence, and to apply these approaches to biomedical and epidemiological data. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, an interest in self-development, and the ability to work in a multidisciplinary research environment are expected.
In accordance with the MSCA mobility rule, applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Finland for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding 1 March 2027. Compulsory national service and/or short stays such as holidays and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered.
An applicant must have completed a relevant Master’s degree before the starting date of employment.
We offer
We offer a three-year Doctoral Candidate position placed at Tampere University within the EU-funded MSCA Doctoral Network DETECTIVE.  A trial period of six (6) months applies to all our new employees.   The salary will be set in accordance with MSCA rates. Target degree is PhD degree from Tampere University, Finland.
The doctoral researcher has the opportunity to work with unique longitudinal biological samples and epidemiological data from the Finnish DIPP study, covering more than three decades of enterovirus circulation.
In addition, interdisciplinary network-wide training schools (one week each):
foundations in virology, bioinformatics and epidemiology;
advanced integration of scientific, diagnostic and public health virology, and
translational virology and connecting academia, clinical practice and public health for pandemic preparedness.
Also DC will have individually tailored career development plan and personal empowerment program.
Tampere University offers a wide range of other staff benefits too, such as occupational health care, access to the campus sport services at a personnel price, flexible working hours, and several restaurants and cafés on campus with staff discounts.  Read more about working at Tampere University:
https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau/work-with-us.
Tampere University (TAU), founded in 1925, is an internationally oriented research university with a strong focus on multidisciplinary research and education at the intersection of technology, health, and society. With ten schools, approximately 23,200 students and 4,200 staff members, including around 330 professors, TAU is the second-largest university in Finland and provides a dynamic and international environment for high-quality research and doctoral education. Read more about Tampere University
https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau/about-tampere-university
and work in Tampere
https://workintampere.fi/.
TAU offers excellent research infrastructure for virology, metagenomics, and environmental research. The available facilities include a dedicated metagenomics core facility, an extensive environmental wastewater sample and data bank, Biosafety Level 2 and 3 laboratories, and dedicated clean areas for PCR and cell culture work. Researchers also have access to a broad range of university-wide core facilities and services through the
TAU Met-Core Facilities and Services
. The virology research environment is further supported by a large collection of wild-type enteroviruses isolated from different countries and continents.
The virus laboratory participates in international quality-control programmes, including QCMD, ensuring high standards in molecular virology and diagnostic research. Extensive high-performance computing resources are available through
CSC – IT Center for Science
, providing the computational capacity required for large-scale sequencing, bioinformatic, and metagenomic analyses.

Please note that the applicant must fill in and complete the
DETECTIVE application form
and provide the following documents:

Details for two references

, please contact:   Assoc. Prof. Sami Oikarinen, email: firstname.lastname@tuni.fi

Haemme
väitöskirjatutkijaa
DETECTIVE-hankkeeseen (Data-driven Excellence in Training of Epidemiological, Clinical, Technological and Innovative Virus Experts), joka on Horizon Europe -ohjelman Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network -verkosto. Verkosto kokoaa yhteen eurooppalaisia akateemisia, kliinisiä, kansanterveyden ja teollisuuden toimijoita kouluttamaan uuden sukupolven asiantuntijoita epidemioiden ennakointiin, uusien virusten seurantaan ja pandemioihin varautumiseen.
Tampereen yliopistossa toteutettavassa väitöskirjaprojektissa tutkitaan virusten väestötason kiertoa ja epidemioiden dynamiikkaa COVID-19-pandemian aikana ja sen jälkeen. Projektissa kartoitetaan jätevesien viromia hyödyntämällä qPCR-menetelmiä, virusrikastusta ja uuden sukupolven sekvensointia. Tavoitteena on tunnistaa ja seurata kaikkia selkärankaisia tartuttavia viruksia, mukaan lukien ihmisten taudinaiheuttajat ja mahdolliset zoonoottiset virukset. Jätevesiviromidata yhdistetään epidemiologiseen ja muuhun väestötason tietoon, ja hankkeessa kehitetään bioinformatiikan menetelmiä sekä dataohjattuja malleja epidemioiden ennustamiseen ja kansanterveyden varhaisvaroitusjärjestelmien kehittämiseen.
Hakuohjeet
Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävästä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta.
Hakuaika tehtävään päättyy
8.10.2026.

ai.summary: Three-year MSCA Doctoral Network position at Tampere University studying viral epidemiology through wastewater-based surveillance, combining molecular virology, high-throughput sequencing, bioinformatics, and machine learning to develop epidemic prediction models.

thematic_fit.rationale: Core research is virology, epidemiology, and public health surveillance. The profile's domains centre on human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, and collaborative systems. No thematic overlap. While both could be framed as addressing real-world challenges, the research questions, methods, and populations studied are entirely different.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both involve data analysis and bioinformatics pipelines, and the position requires Python and machine learning skills, which the profile lists at beginner level with no substantial project experience. However, the methodologies diverge sharply: DETECTIVE focuses on molecular biology, high-throughput sequencing data processing, epidemiological modelling, and time-series analysis. The profile's strengths are in experimental design for user studies, qualitative/quantitative HCI research, and collaborative system evaluation—fundamentally different research practices.

growth_value.rationale: This role would develop substantial Python/bioinformatics expertise, machine learning for time-series prediction, and work with large biological datasets. These are valuable general research skills but orthogonal to human-centred XR, immersive learning, or spatial cognition research. No capability gaps relevant to target identity would be closed.

strategic_value.rationale: Tampere University is a priority-2 target institution, offering European presence and reasonable prestige. DETECTIVE is a well-funded MSCA Doctoral Network with strong international partnerships (UoG, QCMD, multiple institutions) and excellent mobility/training opportunities. This provides genuine research maturity and career development. However, the research domain (virology/epidemiology) is orthogonal to human-centred XR. Supervisors (Oikarinen, Da Silva Filipe) are virologists, not HCI researchers; mentorship would not support target identity development.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed relevant Master's degree (biomedical sciences, bioinformatics, microbiology, virology, immunology, epidemiology, or related field) before starting employment. Candidate holds MSc by Research in progress (Multimedia University, Faculty of Creative Multimedia)—eligibility depends on whether the degree is classified as relevant by DETECTIVE admissions and whether it will be completed by the start date (unclear from posting).

MSCA mobility rule: applicant must not have resided or carried out main activity in Finland for >12 months in the 36 months before 1 March 2027. Candidate is currently in Malaysia; no conflict if the rule is interpreted as residency-based.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: virology and epidemiology have no research continuity with human-centred immersive systems or learning science.

Degree eligibility unclear: candidate's MSc is in Creative Multimedia, not biomedical/bioinformatics sciences. DETECTIVE explicitly lists required disciplines; Creative Multimedia may not be classified as 'related field' by admissions.
Career trajectory risk: accepting a virology PhD would signal a complete pivot away from HCI/XR and make future returns to target identity very difficult.
Supervisor expertise is virological; no HCI or immersive systems mentorship available.
International secondments are in virology/diagnostics (UoG-CVR, QCMD), not in immersive systems or HCI.
